exposure: Medical factors (diabetes, hypertension, prepregnancy obesity, BMI)
cohort: The participants were women with term, singleton hospital births who had one prior cesarean, using 2016 birth certificate data.
finding: The study found significant racial/ethnic differences in how medical factors (hypertension, obesity) and socioeconomic status (insurance type) were associated with the probabilities of TOLAC and VBAC.
mod_finding: Hypertension and obesity were more strongly related to reduced chances of TOLAC and VBAC among White women compared to women of color, and out-of-pocket payment for birth increased TOLAC probability for White women but decreased it for Black women.
